entries.sanskrit: त्रयोदशे सिसृक्षायां मनोर् आकस्मिकाप्लुताम् । धराम् उद्धर्तुम् उद्भूतात् क्रोडाद् दैत्यानुसूदनम् ॥
entries.literal_english: In the thirteenth chapter, when Manu desired creation, the destroyer of the demons arose as a boar to lift the earth.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: trayodaśe sisṛkṣāyāṃ manor ākasmikāplutām | dharām uddhartum udbhūtāt kroḍād daityānusūdanam ||

entries.sanskrit: स्वयम्भुवः पुत्रस् तद्-देहांशत्वात् ॥२॥
word_for_word: because he is a portion of that body
entries.literal_english: He is the son of Svayambhū because he is a portion of that body.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: svayambhuvaḥ putras tad-dehāṃśatvāt ||2||

entries.sanskrit: विष्वक्सेनो हरिर् एवाश्रयो यस्य सः ।
entries.literal_english: He whose shelter is Viṣvaksena—he is Hari himself.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: viṣvakseno harir evāśrayo yasya saḥ |

entries.sanskrit: अतस् तस्य चरितं श्रोतव्यम् इत्य् आह---सुचिरं श्रमो यस्मिंस्, तस्य पुंसां श्रुतस्याञ्जसा मुख्यत्वेनायम् एवार्थः । ईडितः स्तुतः । ननु मुकुन्द-पादारविन्दं येषां हृदयेष्व् अस्ति, तेषां भागवतानां गुणानुश्रवणम् इति यत् ॥४॥
word_for_word: as the principal meaning of what is heard
whose hearts contain Mukunda’s lotus feet
entries.literal_english: Therefore his deeds should be heard. The sense of what is heard is easily understood as the principal subject of the devotees’ hearing: he is the one praised. The reference is to the devotees’ hearing of the Lord’s qualities, for Mukunda’s lotus feet are present in their hearts.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: atas tasya caritaṃ śrotavyam ity āha---suciraṃ śramo yasmiṃs, tasya puṃsāṃ śrutasyāñjasā mukhyatvenāyam evārthaḥ | īḍitaḥ stutaḥ | nanu mukunda-pādāravindaṃ yeṣāṃ hṛdayeṣv asti, teṣāṃ bhāgavatānāṃ guṇānuśravaṇam iti yat ||4||

entries.sanskrit: सहस्र-शीर्षा श्री-कृष्णस् तच्-चरणाव् उपधीयेते यस्मिन्, श्री-कृष्णः प्रीत्या यस्योत्सङ्गे चरणौ प्रसारयतीत्य् अर्थः । तम् अभ्यचष्ट अभ्यभाष्त । मुनिर् मैत्रेयः । प्रणीयमानस् तेन प्रवर्त्यमानः ॥५॥
word_for_word: upon whom his feet are placed
out of affection upon whose lap he stretches his feet
entries.literal_english: The thousand-headed one is Śrī Kṛṣṇa, whose feet are placed upon him; Śrī Kṛṣṇa stretches his feet upon whose lap out of affection. Maitreya the sage addressed him. Praṇīyamāna means being impelled or prompted by him.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: sahasra-śīrṣā śrī-kṛṣṇas tac-caraṇāv upadhīyete yasmin, śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ prītyā yasyotsaṅge caraṇau prasārayatīty arthaḥ | tam abhyacaṣṭa abhyabhāṣta | munir maitreyaḥ | praṇīyamānas tena pravartyamānaḥ ||5||

entries.sanskrit: वेद-गर्भं ब्रह्माणम् ॥६॥
entries.literal_english: Brahmā, whose womb is the Veda.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: veda-garbhaṃ brahmāṇam ||6||

entries.sanskrit: त्वम् एवैकः पिता सर्वेषाम् । यतो जन्म-कृद् वृत्ति-दः पोषकश् च त्वम् एव । अतस् तव यद्य् अप्य् अन्यापेक्षा नास्त्य् अथाप्य् अस्माकं ते शुश्रूषा केन कर्मणा भवेत् तद् विधेहीत्य् उत्तरेणान्वयः ॥७॥
word_for_word: you alone are the father of all
you have no need of anyone else
asmākaṃ te śuśrūṣā kena karmaṇā bhavet
by what service of ours may there be service to you
entries.literal_english: You alone are the father of all, for you alone create, provide livelihood and nourish. Although you have no need of anyone else, tell us what service we may perform for you; that is the connection with the following verse.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: tvam evaikaḥ pitā sarveṣām | yato janma-kṛd vṛtti-daḥ poṣakaś ca tvam eva | atas tava yady apy anyāpekṣā nāsty athāpy asmākaṃ te śuśrūṣā kena karmaṇā bhavet tad vidhehīty uttareṇānvayaḥ ||7||

entries.sanskrit: हे ईड्य, आत्म-शक्तिष्व् अस्मच्-छक्येषु कर्मसु मध्ये केन कर्मणा भवेत् तद् विधेहि इदं कर्तव्यम् इति कथय । यत् कृत्वा यस्मिन् कृते सति । विष्वक् सर्वतः । अमुत्र पर-लोके ॥८॥
word_for_word: among the actions possible through our own powers
by what action it should be
entries.literal_english: O worshipful one, tell us which of the actions possible through our own powers you wish us to perform. Say what should be done—what, once performed, will bring welfare everywhere, including the next world.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: he īḍya, ātma-śaktiṣv asmac-chakyeṣu karmasu madhye kena karmaṇā bhavet tad vidhehi idaṃ kartavyam iti kathaya | yat kṛtvā yasmin kṛte sati | viṣvak sarvataḥ | amutra para-loke ||8||

entries.sanskrit: वां युवाभ्यां स्वस्ति भद्रं स्तात् भूयात् । यद् यतो मा मां शाध्य् अनुशिक्षयेत्य् आत्मना स्वयम् एवार्पितं निवेदितम् अतः प्रीतोऽस्मि ॥९॥
word_for_word: may there be welfare and auspiciousness
entries.literal_english: May there be welfare and auspiciousness for both of you. I am pleased because you have offered yourselves to me, saying, “Instruct and teach us personally whatever you wish.”
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: vāṃ yuvābhyāṃ svasti bhadraṃ stāt bhūyāt | yad yato mā māṃ śādhy anuśikṣayety ātmanā svayam evārpitaṃ niveditam ataḥ prīto’smi ||9||

entries.sanskrit: अपचितिः पूजा । गृह्येत आज्ञेति शेषः । सनकादयो न कुर्वन्ति वयं किम् इति करिष्याम इत्य् एवं-भूतो गतो मत्सरो येभ्यः ॥१०॥
word_for_word: ‘may the command be received’ is understood
Sanaka and the others do not act
entries.literal_english: Apaciti means worship. “May the command be received” is understood. The envy that arose from thinking, “Sanaka and the others do not act—what shall we do?” has disappeared from them.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: apacitiḥ pūjā | gṛhyeta ājñeti śeṣaḥ | sanakādayo na kurvanti vayaṃ kim iti kariṣyāma ity evaṃ-bhūto gato matsaro yebhyaḥ ||10||

entries.sanskrit: गां शास शाधि पालयेत्य् अर्थः । पुरुषं हरिम् ॥११॥
entries.literal_english: Rule and protect the earth; the person to be served is Hari.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: gāṃ śāsa śādhi pālayety arthaḥ | puruṣaṃ harim ||11||

entries.sanskrit: प्रजा-पालकस्य ते तुष्टो भविष्यति ॥१२॥
word_for_word: of you, the protector of the people
entries.literal_english: The Lord, protector of the people, will be pleased with you.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: prajā-pālakasya te tuṣṭo bhaviṣyati ||12||

entries.sanskrit: उदासीनस्य भगवतोऽतोषे मे को दोषः ? तत्राह---येषाम् इति । यज्ञ-लिङ्गो यज्ञ-मूर्तिः । अपगतोऽर्थो यस्मात् । केवलं श्रमायैवेत्य् अर्थः । यद् यस्माद् आत्मैव स्वयं नादृतः । तस्मिन्न् अतुष्टे स्वार्थस्यैवासिद्धेः सर्वात्मत्वाच् च तस्य ॥१३॥
word_for_word: what fault is there in me
from whom independent purpose has departed
the Self alone has not been honored
because one’s own purpose is unfulfilled
and because he is the Self of all
entries.literal_english: What fault is there in my being displeased with the indifferent Lord? The answer is: “of whom.” He has the form of sacrifice, and from him all independent purpose has departed; the effort would be merely labor. Since the Self alone has not been honored, when he is not pleased one’s own purpose is unfulfilled, and he is the Self of all.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: udāsīnasya bhagavato’toṣe me ko doṣaḥ ? tatrāha---yeṣām iti | yajña-liṅgo yajña-mūrtiḥ | apagato’rtho yasmāt | kevalaṃ śramāyaivety arthaḥ | yad yasmād ātmaiva svayaṃ nādṛtaḥ | tasminn atuṣṭe svārthasyaivāsiddheḥ sarvātmatvāc ca tasya ||13||

entries.sanskrit: वर्तेय वर्तिष्ये । अमीवसूदन पाप-नाशन । अनुजानीद्यत्र स्थातव्यम् इत्य् अनुज्ञां देहि ॥१४॥
entries.literal_english: Varteya means “I should live” or “I shall live.” O destroyer of evil, O destroyer of sin, give us permission to remain wherever we ought to remain.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: varteya vartiṣye | amīvasūdana pāpa-nāśana | anujānīdyatra sthātavyam ity anujñāṃ dehi ||14||

entries.sanskrit: महीति चेद् अत आह---यदोकः स्थानं सा मही । हे देव, अस्या देव्याः ।
word_for_word: the earth is the place of habitation
entries.literal_english: If one asks, “Why earth?”, the answer is: the earth is the place of habitation. O Lord, this goddess is yours.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: mahīti ced ata āha---yadokaḥ sthānaṃ sā mahī | he deva, asyā devyāḥ |

entries.sanskrit: पूर्वं पाने कृतेऽपि पुनर् अकाण्ड एवोद्भूतानाम् अपां मध्ये सन्नाम् अवसन्नां निमग्नाम् । समुन्नेष्ये उद्धरिष्यामि ॥१६॥
entries.literal_english: Although the waters had previously been drunk, she had again become submerged and sunk in the suddenly arisen waters. I shall lift her up.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: pūrvaṃ pāne kṛte’pi punar akāṇḍa evodbhūtānām apāṃ madhye sannām avasannāṃ nimagnām | samunneṣye uddhariṣyāmi ||16||

entries.sanskrit: चिन्ताम् एवाह---सृजतः सतः । वर्भिर् अद्भिः । रसां रसा-तलम् । ईश्वरेण सर्गे नियुक्तैः मेऽनुष्ठेयं स एव विदधातु सम्पादयतु ॥१७॥
word_for_word: appointed by the Lord to creation
entries.literal_english: He describes his thought: “I am creating the existent world.” The waters are the waters of the ocean; rasā means the lower region, Rasātala. The Lord, who appointed me to creation, should himself accomplish what I must do.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: cintām evāha---sṛjataḥ sataḥ | varbhir adbhiḥ | rasāṃ rasā-talam | īśvareṇa sarge niyuktaiḥ me’nuṣṭheyaṃ sa eva vidadhātu sampādayatu ||17||

entries.sanskrit: वराह-तोकः सूक्ष्मो वराहः । ख-स्थ आकाशे स्थितः सन् ॥१८॥
entries.literal_english: A young boar means a small boar. He stood in the sky.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: varāha-tokaḥ sūkṣmo varāhaḥ | kha-stha ākāśe sthitaḥ san ||18||

entries.literal_english: No commentary

entries.sanskrit: चित्रधा अनेकधा ॥२०॥
entries.literal_english: Citradhā means in many ways.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: citradhā anekadhā ||20||

entries.sanskrit: न व्याख्यातम्。
entries.literal_english: No commentary

entries.sanskrit: पूर्वम् अङ्गुष्ठाग्र-प्रमाणो दृष्टः । गण्ड-शिला स्थूल-पाषाणस् तत् समः । यज्ञो विष्णुः । निज-रूप-तिरो-धानेन मे मनः खेदयन् ॥२२॥
word_for_word: first the size of a thumb
entries.literal_english: He had first been seen only the size of a thumb; then he became as large as a massive rock. Yajña means Viṣṇu. By concealing his own form, he was troubling my mind.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: pūrvam aṅguṣṭhāgra-pramāṇo dṛṣṭaḥ | gaṇḍa-śilā sthūla-pāṣāṇas tat samaḥ | yajño viṣṇuḥ | nija-rūpa-tiro-dhānena me manaḥ khedayan ||22||

entries.sanskrit: इति मीमांस-मानस्य सतः । जगर्जागर्जत् । गिरीन्द्र-तुल्यः ॥२३॥
word_for_word: equal to the lord of mountains
entries.literal_english: While Brahmā was considering in this way, the Lord Yajña-Puruṣa roared. Jagarja means “he roared”; he was equal to the lord of mountains.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: iti mīmāṃsa-mānasya sataḥ | jagarjāgarjat | girīndra-tulyaḥ ||23||

entries.sanskrit: स्वेन असाधारणेन गर्जितेन ॥२४॥
entries.literal_english: With his own extraordinary roar.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: svena asādhāraṇena garjitena ||24||

entries.sanskrit: घर्घरितं तज्-जात्य्-अनुकरण-ध्वनिम् । अनिश्चयेन यः स्व-खेदस् तस्य क्षयिष्णु क्षपयिष्णु नाशकम् । ते इति पुनर् उक्तिः प्रसिद्धि-ख्यापनार्था । त्रिभिः पवित्रैर् ऋग्-यजुः-साम-मन्त्रैर् अगृणन्न् अस्तुवन् ॥२५॥
word_for_word: the Ṛg, Yajur and Sāma mantras
entries.literal_english: Gharghara means the imitation of the sound characteristic of that animal. His roar destroys the sorrow caused by uncertainty. The repeated “they” indicates renown: with the three purifying Vedic mantras of Ṛg, Yajur and Sāma they praised him.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: ghargharitaṃ taj-jāty-anukaraṇa-dhvanim | aniścayena yaḥ sva-khedas tasya kṣayiṣṇu kṣapayiṣṇu nāśakam | te iti punar uktiḥ prasiddhi-khyāpanārthā | tribhiḥ pavitrair ṛg-yajuḥ-sāma-mantrair agṛṇann astuvan ||25||

entries.sanskrit: वेदैर् वितन्यते स्तूयते मूर्तिर् यस्य सः । अत एवात्मनो गुणान् अनुवदति तथा तत् तेषां ब्रह्म उच्चारितं वेदम् अवधार्य ज्ञात्वा ॥२६॥
word_for_word: whose form is expanded and praised by the Vedas
understanding the Brahman, the Veda, of those qualities
entries.literal_english: He whose form is expanded and praised by the Vedas. Therefore he recites his own qualities, and, understanding the Brahman—the Veda—uttered by those qualities, he praises him.

transliteration: vedair vitanyate stūyate mūrtir yasya saḥ | ata evātmano guṇān anuvadati tathā tat teṣāṃ brahma uccāritaṃ vedam avadhārya jñātvā ||26||

entries.sanskrit: कथं-भूतः सन्न् आविवेश ? इत्य् अपेक्षायाम् आह द्वाभ्याम् । उच्चैः क्षिप्तो वालः पुच्छं येन । ख-चर आकाश-चारी । कथोरः कठिनः । सटाः स्कन्ध-वालान् । खराणि तीक्ष्णानि रोमाणि यस्याः सा त्वग्यस्य । खुरैर् आहतान्य् अभ्राणि येन । सित-दंष्ट्रोऽति-शुक्ल-दंष्ट्रः । ईक्षा निरीक्षणम् एव ज्योतिर् आलोको यस्य । तदा प्रकाशान्तराभावात् । बभासेऽशोभत । मही-ध्रः पृथिव्या उद्धर्ता ॥२७॥
word_for_word: the clouds struck by his hooves
entries.literal_english: The question “How did he enter?” is answered by two verses. His tail was raised high; he moved through the sky; he was hard and had bristles on his shoulders and tail; his hide had sharp hairs; the clouds were struck by his hooves; his tusks were brilliant white; his gaze itself was light. Since there was no other illumination, he shone as the lifter of the earth.

transliteration: kathaṃ-bhūtaḥ sann āviveśa ? ity apekṣāyām āha dvābhyām | uccaiḥ kṣipto vālaḥ pucchaṃ yena | kha-cara ākāśa-cārī | kathoraḥ kaṭhinaḥ | saṭāḥ skandha-vālān | kharāṇi tīkṣṇāni romāṇi yasyāḥ sā tvagyasya | khurair āhatāny abhrāṇi yena | sita-daṃṣṭro’ti-śukla-daṃṣṭraḥ | īkṣā nirīkṣaṇam eva jyotir āloko yasya | tadā prakāśāntarābhāvāt | babhāse’śobhata | mahī-dhraḥ pṛthivyā uddhartā ||27||

entries.sanskrit: क्रोडापदेशो वराह-च्छड्मा । अतः स्वयम् अध्वराङ्गोऽपि पशुर् इव घ्राणेन विजिघ्रन् । गृणतः स्तोतॄन् विप्रान् उद्वीक्ष्योर्ध्वं वीक्ष्य कं जलम् आविशत् ॥२८॥
word_for_word: though himself a limb of sacrifice
sniffing with his nose like an animal
entries.literal_english: Kroḍa is a designation for a boar, a disguise assumed by the Lord. Therefore, though he himself is an embodied limb of the sacrifice, he sniffed like an animal; he looked upward at the praising brāhmaṇas and entered the water.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: kroḍāpadeśo varāha-cchaḍmā | ataḥ svayam adhvarāṅgo’pi paśur iva ghrāṇena vijighran | gṛṇataḥ stotṝn viprān udvīkṣyordhvaṃ vīkṣya kaṃ jalam āviśat ||28||

entries.sanskrit: तदानीन्तन-समुद्र-ध्वनिम् उत्प्रेक्षते । स उदन्वान् समुद्र आर्त इव स्तनयन् शब्दं कुर्वन् भो यज्ञेश्वर, मा मां पाहि माम् अव इत्य् एवं चुक्रोश । आर्त-सादृश्यम् आह---उत्सृष्टाः प्रसारिता दीर्घा ऊर्मय एव भुजास् तैर् विशिष्टः । आर्तत्वे हेतुः, वज्र-कूटो वज्र-मयः पर्वतस् तद्वद् अङ्गं यद् भगवतस् तस्य निपात-वेगेन विशीर्णा कुक्षिर् यस्य ॥२९॥
word_for_word: the ocean’s sound at that time
the ocean thundered as though distressed
with belly shattered by the force of his fall
entries.literal_english: The verse imagines the sound of the ocean at that time. The ocean thundered as though distressed, crying, “O Lord of sacrifice, protect me!” Its long waves were like outstretched arms. The reason for its distress was that its belly was shattered by the impact of the Lord’s fall, like a mountain of adamant.

transliteration: tadānīntana-samudra-dhvanim utprekṣate | sa udanvān samudra ārta iva stanayan śabdaṃ kurvan bho yajñeśvara, mā māṃ pāhi mām ava ity evaṃ cukrośa | ārta-sādṛśyam āha---utsṛṣṭāḥ prasāritā dīrghā ūrmaya eva bhujās tair viśiṣṭaḥ | ārtatve hetuḥ, vajra-kūṭo vajra-mayaḥ parvatas tadvad aṅgaṃ yad bhagavatas tasya nipāta-vegena viśīrṇā kukṣir yasya ||29||

entries.sanskrit: तदा रसायां रसातले गां पृथ्वीं ददर्श । कः ? त्रि-परुः त्रीणि परूंषि सवनात्मकानि पर्वाणि यस्य । यज्ञ-मूर्तिर् इत्य् अर्थः । किं कुर्वन् ? क्षुर-प्रा आयताग्राः शरास् तत् सदृशैः खुरैर् अपो दरयन् । कथम् ? उत्पार-पारम् उत्पाराणां पार-शून्यानाम् अप्य् अपां पारम-वसानं यथा भवति तथा विदारयन् । कथं-भूतः ? अग्रे प्रलय-समये तत्र तास्व् अप्सु सुषुप्सुः शिशयिषुः सन् जीवा धीयन्ते यस्यां सर्व-जीवाधार-भूतां यां स्वयम् अभ्यधत्त आभिमुख्येन दधार । जठरे धृतवान् इत्य् अर्थः । अनेन तद् उद्धरणेऽनायासं द्योतयति ॥३०॥
word_for_word: then he saw the earth in Rasātala
hooves whose tips are like arrows
to the end of even boundless waters
the support of all living beings
entries.literal_english: Then, in Rasātala, he saw the earth. He is called tri-paru because he has three sacrificial joints, and thus is the sacrificial form. He split the waters with hooves whose tips were long like arrows, cutting through them until even the boundless waters had an end. He carried in his belly the earth that holds all beings, where living beings lie asleep at the end of the dissolution. This shows that lifting her was effortless for him.

transliteration: tadā rasāyāṃ rasātale gāṃ pṛthvīṃ dadarśa | kaḥ ? tri-paruḥ trīṇi parūṃṣi savanātmakāni parvāṇi yasya | yajña-mūrtir ity arthaḥ | kiṃ kurvan ? kṣura-prā āyatāgrāḥ śarās tat sadṛśaiḥ khurair apo darayan | katham ? utpāra-pāram utpārāṇāṃ pāra-śūnyānām apy apāṃ pārama-vasānaṃ yathā bhavati tathā vidārayan | kathaṃ-bhūtaḥ ? agre pralaya-samaye tatra tāsv apsu suṣupsuḥ śiśayiṣuḥ san jīvā dhīyante yasyāṃ sarva-jīvādhāra-bhūtāṃ yāṃ svayam abhyadhatta ābhimukhyena dadhāra | jaṭhare dhṛtavān ity arthaḥ | anena tad uddharaṇe’nāyāsaṃ dyotayati ||30||

entries.sanskrit: रसायाः सकाशाद् उत्थितः संरुरुचे सम्यग् अशोभत । तत्राप्य् अम्भसि गदाम् उद्यम्यागच्छन्तं रुन्धानं प्रतिघ्नन्तं न सह्यः सहनानर्हो विक्रमो यस्य तं दैत्यं सुनाभं चक्रं तद्वत् सन्दीपितस् तीव्रो मन्युर् यस्य । यद् वा, मयि विद्यमाने किम् इति परिभवं सहस इति सुनाभेन सन्दीपितस् तीव्र-मन्युः स भगवान् सिंहो गजम् इव लीलया जघानेत्य् उत्तरेणान्वयः ॥३१॥ गजेन्द्रो जगतीं क्रीडया विदारयन् गैरिकया यथा अरुण-गण्ड-तुण्डो भवति तथा तस्य रक्तम् एव पङ्कस् तेनाङ्कितौ गण्डौ तुण्डं च यस्य सः ॥३२॥
word_for_word: the demon coming with a mace
whose anger was kindled like the Sudarśana wheel
sih o gajam iva līlayā jaghāna
he slew him playfully as a lion an elephant
entries.literal_english: He rose from the Rasā waters and shone beautifully. In those waters he met the demon who came against him with a mace; his irresistible power was like an obstacle, and his intense anger was kindled like the Sudarśana wheel. Since the Lord was present, the demon dared to insult him; the Lord, with fierce anger, slew him playfully as a lion kills an elephant. As an elephant tears the earth in sport and becomes red-faced from the red mineral, so the Lord’s cheeks and snout were marked with the demon’s blood.

transliteration: rasāyāḥ sakāśād utthitaḥ saṃruruce samyag aśobhata | tatrāpy ambhasi gadām udyamyāgacchantaṃ rundhānaṃ pratighnantaṃ na sahyaḥ sahanānarho vikramo yasya taṃ daityaṃ sunābhaṃ cakraṃ tadvat sandīpitas tīvro manyur yasya | yad vā, mayi vidyamāne kim iti paribhavaṃ sahasa iti sunābhena sandīpitas tīvra-manyuḥ sa bhagavān siṃho gajam iva līlayā jaghānety uttareṇānvayaḥ ||31|| gajendro jagatīṃ krīḍayā vidārayan gairikayā yathā aruṇa-gaṇḍa-tuṇḍo bhavati tathā tasya raktam eva paṅkas tenāṅkitau gaṇḍau tuṇḍaṃ ca yasya saḥ ||32||

entries.sanskrit: प्रज्ञाय आलक्ष्य । अनुवाको वैदिकं सूक्तं तत् सदृशैर् वाक्यैस् तुष्टुवुः ॥३३॥
entries.literal_english: Prājñāya means having recognized or perceived. They praised him with words resembling a Vedic hymn.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: prajñāya ālakṣya | anuvāko vaidikaṃ sūktaṃ tat sadṛśair vākyais tuṣṭuvuḥ ||33||

entries.sanskrit: भो अजित ! ते त्वया जितं जितम् इति सम्भ्रमे वीप्सा । यज्ञैर् भाव्यते आक्रियत इति तथा । त्रयीं वेद-मयीम् । निलिल्युर् लीन-प्रायाः । कारणं पृथिव्य्-उद्धरणं तेन सूकराय ॥३४॥
entries.literal_english: “O unconquered one, you have indeed conquered!” The repetition expresses excitement. He is made manifest through sacrifices, and he is the threefold Veda. They were almost absorbed in him. Because he lifted the earth, the cause of this praise is his boar form.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: bho ajita ! te tvayā jitaṃ jitam iti sambhrame vīpsā | yajñair bhāvyate ākriyata iti tathā | trayīṃ veda-mayīm | nililyur līna-prāyāḥ | kāraṇaṃ pṛthivy-uddharaṇaṃ tena sūkarāya ||34||

entries.sanskrit: यज्ञात्मतां प्रपञ्चयन्तः स्तुवन्ति---रूपम् इत्य्-आदि-चतुर्भिः । छन्दांसि गायत्र्य्-आदीनि । यज्ञाङ्ग-भूत-च्छन्द-आद्य्-अनुवादेन भगवद् अवयवता विधीयते । बर्हिः-शब्दे दीर्घाभाव आर्षः । दृशि चक्षुषि । चातुर्-होत्रं होत्रादि-कर्म-चतुष्टयम् ॥३५॥
word_for_word: expanding the idea that he is sacrifice
entries.literal_english: They praise him by expanding the idea that he is sacrifice. The metres beginning with Gāyatrī are identified with his limbs by transferring the names of the metres and other parts of sacrifice to his body. The form “barhis” without the long vowel is an ancient usage. Dṛśi means the eyes. Cātur-hotram means the fourfold work beginning with the hotṛ.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: yajñātmatāṃ prapañcayantaḥ stuvanti---rūpam ity-ādi-caturbhiḥ | chandāṃsi gāyatry-ādīni | yajñāṅga-bhūta-cchanda-ādy-anuvādena bhagavad avayavatā vidhīyate | barhiḥ-śabde dīrghābhāva ārṣaḥ | dṛśi cakṣuṣi | cātur-hotraṃ hotrādi-karma-catuṣṭayam ||35||

entries.sanskrit: स्रुक् जुहूस् तुण्डे मुखाग्रे । स्रुवो नासिकयोः । इडा भक्षण-पात्री । चमसा ग्रहाश् च सोम-पात्राणि । प्राशित्रं ब्रह्म-भाग-पात्रम् । ग्रस्यतेऽनेनेति ग्रसनं मुखान्तर्वर्ति-च्छिद्रम् । चर्वणं भक्षणम् ॥३६॥
word_for_word: the sruc and juhū are in the snout
the sruva vessels are the nostrils
the vessel for the Brahmā priest’s portion
the inner opening of the mouth
entries.literal_english: The srucc and juhū are at the tip of his snout; the sruva vessels are his nostrils; iḍā is the vessel for food; camasas and grahas are the vessels for Soma; prāśitra is the vessel for the Brahmā priest’s portion; grāsana is the inner opening of the mouth through which food is swallowed; and carvaṇa is chewing.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: sruk juhūs tuṇḍe mukhāgre | sruvo nāsikayoḥ | iḍā bhakṣaṇa-pātrī | camasā grahāś ca soma-pātrāṇi | prāśitraṃ brahma-bhāga-pātram | grasyate’neneti grasanaṃ mukhāntarvarti-cchidram | carvaṇaṃ bhakṣaṇam ||36||

entries.sanskrit: दीक्षा दीक्षणीयेष्टिः । अनुजन्म वारं वारम् अभिव्यक्तिः । उपसदस् तिस्र इष्टयः । शिरो-धरं ग्रीवा । प्रायणीया दीक्षानन्तरेष्टिः । उदयनीया समाप्तीष्टिः । ते एव दंष्ट्रे यस्य । प्रवर्ग्यो महा-वीरः प्रत्युपसदं पूर्वं क्रियते । सत्यो होम-रहितोऽग्निः । आवसथ्य औपासनाग्निः । तयोर् द्वन्द्वैक्यम् । तत् तव क्रतु-रूपस्य शीर्षं शिरः । चितय इष्टका-चयनानि पञ्चासवः प्राणाः ॥३७॥
entries.literal_english: Dīkṣā is the initiating sacrifice; anu-janma is its repeated manifestation; the upasads are three offerings; śiro-dhara means the neck; prāyaṇīya is the offering after initiation, and udayanīya is the concluding offering. The two tusks are the two great sacrificial implements. Pravargya is the mahāvīra rite performed before each upasad. Satya is the fire without oblation; āvasathya is the household fire. Together they form the head of the Lord whose form is sacrifice. The fire-altars are his brick arrangements and the five vital airs are the five piles.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: dīkṣā dīkṣaṇīyeṣṭiḥ | anujanma vāraṃ vāram abhivyaktiḥ | upasadas tisra iṣṭayaḥ | śiro-dharaṃ grīvā | prāyaṇīyā dīkṣānantareṣṭiḥ | udayanīyā samāptīṣṭiḥ | te eva daṃṣṭre yasya | pravargyo mahā-vīraḥ pratyupasadaṃ pūrvaṃ kriyate | satyo homa-rahito’gniḥ | āvasathya aupāsanāgniḥ | tayor dvandvaikyam | tat tava kratu-rūpasya śīrṣaṃ śiraḥ | citaya iṣṭakā-cayanāni pañcāsavaḥ prāṇāḥ ||37||

entries.sanskrit: प्रातः सवनादीन्य् अवस्थितिर् आसनं बाल्याद्य्-अवस्था वा । अग्निष्टोमोऽत्य्-अग्निष्टोम उक्थ्यः षोडशी वाजपेयोऽति-रात्र आप्तोर्याम इति सप्त-संस्थादि-भेदास् त्वङ् मांसादि-सप्त-धातवः । सत्राणि द्वादशाहादीनि बहु-याग-सङ्घात-रूपाणि । असोमा यज्ञाः, स-सोमाः क्रतवः, तद्-रूपस् त्वम् । इष्टिर् यजनम् अनुष्ठानं तद् एव बन्धनं यस्य सः ॥३८॥
entries.literal_english: The morning pressing and the other pressings are his postures—or, alternatively, the stages beginning with childhood. The seven sacrificial institutions—Agniṣṭoma, Atyagniṣṭoma, Ukthya, Ṣoḍaśī, Vājapeya, Atirātra and Aptoryāma—are his seven bodily constituents beginning with skin and flesh. Sattras such as the twelve-day rite are groups of many sacrifices. Soma-less sacrifices and Soma rites are both his forms. Iṣṭi means the act of worship; he whose worship itself is bondage is sacrifice embodied.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: prātaḥ savanādīny avasthitir āsanaṃ bālyādy-avasthā vā | agniṣṭomo’ty-agniṣṭoma ukthyaḥ ṣoḍaśī vājapeyo’ti-rātra āptoryāma iti sapta-saṃsthādi-bhedās tvaṅ māṃsādi-sapta-dhātavaḥ | satrāṇi dvādaśāhādīni bahu-yāga-saṅghāta-rūpāṇi | asomā yajñāḥ, sa-somāḥ kratavaḥ, tad-rūpas tvam | iṣṭir yajanam anuṣṭhānaṃ tad eva bandhanaṃ yasya saḥ ||38||

entries.sanskrit: पूर्वोक्तम् एव स-परिकरं कीर्तयन्तः प्रणमन्ति---नमो नम इति । अखिल-मन्त्रादि-रूपाय क्रियात्मने सामान्य-व्यापार-रूपाय । किं च, वैराग्य-यूक्त-कर्म-साध्या सत्त्व-शुद्धिस् ततो भक्तिस् तत आत्म-जयश् चित्त-स्थैर्यं, तेनानुभावितं साक्षात्-कृतं यज् ज्ञानं तस्मै । एवं-भूत-ज्ञान-प्रदाय गुरवे च ॥३९॥
word_for_word: the previously described form with accessories
whose form is all mantras and rites
entries.literal_english: They bow while praising the previously described form together with all its accessories: “Obeisance, obeisance.” He is the active form of all mantras and related rites, the universal form of action. Through action performed with detachment comes purification of the mind; from that comes devotion; from devotion comes mastery of the self, steadiness of mind, and direct realization of knowledge. They bow to him who gives such knowledge and who is the spiritual teacher.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: pūrvoktam eva sa-parikaraṃ kīrtayantaḥ praṇamanti---namo nama iti | akhila-mantrādi-rūpāya kriyātmane sāmānya-vyāpāra-rūpāya | kiṃ ca, vairāgya-yūkta-karma-sādhyā sattva-śuddhis tato bhaktis tata ātma-jayaś citta-sthairyaṃ, tenānubhāvitaṃ sākṣāt-kṛtaṃ yaj jñānaṃ tasmai | evaṃ-bhūta-jñāna-pradāya gurave ca ||39||

entries.sanskrit: हे भूधर । स-भूधरा स-पर्वता । वनाद् उदकान् निर्गच्छतो गजेन्द्रस्य । दता दन्तेन ॥४०॥
entries.literal_english: O lifter of the earth, together with its mountains. He lifted it from the forest of waters with his tusk.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: he bhūdhara | sa-bhūdharā sa-parvatā | vanād udakān nirgacchato gajendrasya | datā dantena ||40||

entries.sanskrit: त्वया धृता भूर् विराजत इत्य् उक्तम् । इदानीं भू-मण्डलेन त्वद्-रूपं विराजत इत्य् आहुः---त्रयीति । अथेत्य् अर्थान्तरे । ते इदं रूपं दन्तेन धृतं यद् भू-मण्डलं तेन चकास्ति शोभते । शृङ्गेणोढो धृतो यो घनस् तेन । भूयसाऽतिमहता विभ्रमो विलासः ॥४१॥
word_for_word: the earth shines because you support it
like a cloud borne on a horn
entries.literal_english: It was said that the earth shines because you support it. Now they say that your form shines with the earthly sphere: the earthly sphere supported on your tusk shines by that tusk, just as a cloud borne on a horn shines. Its great size gives rise to the Lord’s majestic splendor.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: tvayā dhṛtā bhūr virājata ity uktam | idānīṃ bhū-maṇḍalena tvad-rūpaṃ virājata ity āhuḥ---trayīti | athety arthāntare | te idaṃ rūpaṃ dantena dhṛtaṃ yad bhū-maṇḍalaṃ tena cakāsti śobhate | śṛṅgeṇoḍho dhṛto yo ghanas tena | bhūyasā’timahatā vibhramo vilāsaḥ ||41||

entries.sanskrit: लोकाय वास-स्थानार्थम् । ते पत्नीम् । जगतां मातरम् । यतस् त्वं पितासि । एवं सति तत्र स्थिताः सन्तस् त्वया पित्रा सहास्यै मात्रे मनसा विधेम नमनं करिष्यामः, नमस्कारेण परिचरेमेति वा । स्व-तेजो-धारण-शक्तिं याज्ञिका मन्त्रतोऽग्निम् अरणाव् इवाधाः निहितवान् असि ॥४२॥
word_for_word: for the worlds as a dwelling place
the power of sustaining your radiance
entries.literal_english: For the worlds, as a dwelling place; to you, his wife; the mother of the worlds, because you are their father. Since we reside there, we shall bow to this mother together with you, the father, or we shall serve her through obeisance. You have placed your own power of sustaining radiance, the sacrificial fire, in the fire-sticks through the mantra.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: lokāya vāsa-sthānārtham | te patnīm | jagatāṃ mātaram | yatas tvaṃ pitāsi | evaṃ sati tatra sthitāḥ santas tvayā pitrā sahāsyai mātre manasā vidhema namanaṃ kariṣyāmaḥ, namaskāreṇa paricaremeti vā | sva-tejo-dhāraṇa-śaktiṃ yājñikā mantrato’gnim araṇāv ivādhāḥ nihitavān asi ||42||

entries.sanskrit: इदं च त्वयाति-दुष्करं कृतम् इत्य् आहुः---क इति । प्रभो, तव त्वया कृतं भुव उद्विबर्हणम् उद्धरणं त्वद् अन्यः कः श्रद्दधीत स्पृहयेत् । अध्यवस्येद् इत्य् अर्थः । त्वयि पुनर् असौ विस्मयो न भवति । यतो विश्वे सर्वे विस्मया यस्मिन् । कुतः ? यो भवान् । अतिविस्मयम् अत्यद्भुतम् इदं विश्वम्, क्रिया-विशेषणं वा । ससृजे सृष्टवान् ॥४३॥
word_for_word: this extremely difficult deed was done
who could desire or undertake it
in whom the entire universe is amazing
entries.literal_english: They say that this deed was extremely difficult: who besides you could desire or undertake the lifting of the earth that you performed? You are not amazed by it, because the entire universe is amazing in you. Why? Because you created this supremely wondrous universe.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: idaṃ ca tvayāti-duṣkaraṃ kṛtam ity āhuḥ---ka iti | prabho, tava tvayā kṛtaṃ bhuva udvibarhaṇam uddharaṇaṃ tvad anyaḥ kaḥ śraddadhīta spṛhayet | adhyavasyed ity arthaḥ | tvayi punar asau vismayo na bhavati | yato viśve sarve vismayā yasmin | kutaḥ ? yo bhavān | ativismayam atyadbhutam idaṃ viśvam, kriyā-viśeṣaṇaṃ vā | sasṛje sṛṣṭavān ||43||

entries.sanskrit: विस्मयं दर्शयन्तः प्रार्थयन्ते---विधुन्वतेति द्वाभ्याम् । सटानां शिखाभिर् अग्रैर् उद्धूता उच्छलिता ये शिवा अम्बु-बिन्दवस् तैः सिच्यमाना वयं पवित्री-कृताः ॥४४॥
word_for_word: from the tips of the bristles
entries.literal_english: Displaying their wonder, they pray in two verses. We have been purified by the auspicious drops of water shaken loose and sent upward from the tips of your bristles.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: vismayaṃ darśayantaḥ prārthayante---vidhunvateti dvābhyām | saṭānāṃ śikhābhir agrair uddhūtā ucchalitā ye śivā ambu-bindavas taiḥ sicyamānā vayaṃ pavitrī-kṛtāḥ ||44||

entries.sanskrit: तव कर्मणां पारं य एष तेऽवलोकयति ज्ञातुम् इच्छतीत्य् अर्थः । यस्य तव योग-मायया यो गुणैः सह् योगस् तेन मोहितम् । अतो विश्वस्य शं मङ्गलं विधेहि । यथा त्वाम् अचिन्त्यानन्त-शक्तिं ज्ञात्वा भजे तथानुगृहाणेत्य् अर्थः ॥४५॥
word_for_word: by yoga-māyā through conjunction with the guṇas
you possessed of inconceivable unlimited powers
entries.literal_english: Whoever tries to know the limit of your acts is bewildered by your yoga-māyā, by its conjunction with the guṇas. Therefore grant welfare to the universe. Bless me so that, knowing you as possessed of inconceivable and unlimited powers, I may worship you.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: tava karmaṇāṃ pāraṃ ya eṣa te’valokayati jñātum icchatīty arthaḥ | yasya tava yoga-māyayā yo guṇaiḥ sah yogas tena mohitam | ato viśvasya śaṃ maṅgalaṃ vidhehi | yathā tvām acintyānanta-śaktiṃ jñātvā bhaje tathānugṛhāṇety arthaḥ ||45||

entries.sanskrit: उपस्थीयमानः स्तूयमानः । स्व-खुराक्रान्त इति जलेऽपि धारण-शक्त्य्-आधानं दर्शयति । अविता रक्षकः ॥४६॥
entries.literal_english: He was approached and praised. The phrase “trampled by his own hooves” shows that he endowed even the water with the power to bear him. Avitā means protector.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: upasthīyamānaḥ stūyamānaḥ | sva-khurākrānta iti jale’pi dhāraṇa-śakty-ādhānaṃ darśayati | avitā rakṣakaḥ ||46||

entries.sanskrit: ययौ स्व-लोकम् इति शेषः । अन्तर्दधे इति वा ॥४७॥
word_for_word: he went to his own abode
entries.literal_english: “He went to his own abode” is understood; alternatively, it means “he disappeared.”
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: yayau sva-lokam iti śeṣaḥ | antardadhe iti vā ||47||

entries.sanskrit: कथनीयानि मायीनि मायावन्ति चरित्राणि यस्य । श्रवयेत श्रावयेत । ह्रस्वत्वम् आर्षम् । उशतीं कमनीयाम् । हृदि प्रसीदति स्व-मनसि सन्तुष्यतीत्य् अर्थः ॥४८॥
word_for_word: whose deeds are māyic and worthy of narration
let him cause them to be heard
he is pleased in the heart
entries.literal_english: His deeds are māyic and worthy of narration. Let him cause them to be heard; the short vowel is an ancient usage. Uśatī means beautiful or pleasing. “He is pleased in the heart” means that he becomes satisfied within his own mind.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: kathanīyāni māyīni māyāvanti caritrāṇi yasya | śravayeta śrāvayeta | hrasvatvam ārṣam | uśatīṃ kamanīyām | hṛdi prasīdati sva-manasi santuṣyatīty arthaḥ ||48||

entries.sanskrit: आशिषो यद्य् अपि सुलभास् तथापि न प्रार्थनीया इत्य् आह---ताभिर् आशीर्भिर् अलम् । लवात्मभिस् तुच्छाभिः । न च तदा भजनस्य वैफल्य शङ्कनीयम् इत्य् आह---भगवद्-भजन-व्यतिरेकेण फलान्तर-दृष्टिं विना भजतां स्व-पद-प्राप्तिं स्वयम् एव विधत्ते । गुहाशयत्वाद् अहैतुकीं भक्तिं जानन् ॥४९॥
word_for_word: because he dwells in the heart
entries.literal_english: Although blessings are easily obtained, they should not be requested; enough of such blessings. They are insignificant compared with devotion. One should not fear that worship is fruitless: without showing any separate fruit, the Lord himself grants his own abode to those who worship him. He knows their causeless devotion because he dwells in the heart.
entries.source_note: Pinned source: vishvAsa/purANam_vaiShNavam @ 100560de6c9f68c2875097d40a2012a84c784179; exact Śrīdhara source block restored and fully translated.
transliteration: āśiṣo yady api sulabhās tathāpi na prārthanīyā ity āha---tābhir āśīrbhir alam | lavātmabhis tucchābhiḥ | na ca tadā bhajanasya vaiphalya śaṅkanīyam ity āha---bhagavad-bhajana-vyatirekeṇa phalāntara-dṛṣṭiṃ vinā bhajatāṃ sva-pada-prāptiṃ svayam eva vidhatte | guhāśayatvād ahaitukīṃ bhaktiṃ jānan ||49||

entries.sanskrit: अतः को नाम पुरा-कथानां पूर्व-वृत्तानां मध्ये कथञ्चिद् आपीय विरज्येत विरमेत् । नरेतरं पशुं विना ॥५०॥
word_for_word: of ancient accounts of past events
except an animal rather than a human
entries.literal_english: Therefore who, except an animal rather than a human being, would hear even a little of these ancient accounts of past events and then turn away?

transliteration: ataḥ ko nāma purā-kathānāṃ pūrva-vṛttānāṃ madhye kathañcid āpīya virajyeta viramet | naretaraṃ paśuṃ vinā ||50||
